scenes.heading: Handling revisions and client feedback professionally

sents.d: Handling revisions and client feedback professionally
Structured feedback rounds keep projects on track and on budget.

Open-ended feedback requests ('let me know what you think') often produce vague responses that are hard to act on — asking specific questions instead ('does this match the tone you wanted? is anything unclear?') tends to get more usable feedback.
Defining a specific number of revision rounds in the contract, with additional rounds billed separately, protects against a project quietly expanding into unlimited free rewrites.

When feedback feels like a completely new direction rather than a refinement of the original brief, naming that plainly and discussing whether it falls under the original scope keeps the relationship professional rather than resentful.

take: Ask targeted feedback questions and keep revisions in scope.
